complexity.notes: Correct but slow: each edge removal calls prerequisites.remove([v, w]), an O(E) scan, and building the start list does an O(V) scan per prerequisite, so the whole run is O(E^2 + V*E). It also mutates the input list, which is avoidable. O(V + E) is achievable with ||Kahn's algorithm: an in-degree count array plus a queue of zero-in-degree courses, decrementing counts instead of scanning lists||. The dict keys are consecutive course labels, so hashing is not adversarially exploitable here.
complexity.summary: A reverse topological peel: it builds prerequisite and dependent adjacency lists, starts from courses that nothing depends on, and removes edges one at a time as each course's dependents are resolved, returning whether every edge was eliminated. The per-edge work uses linear list scans (prerequisites.remove, starts.remove, list membership), which makes it quadratic rather than linear.
